review_locator: PMCID:PMC2884560, GDNF family; PMCID:PMC7619074, RET receptor tyrosine kinase architecture, assemblies and activation
primary_title: Cryo-EM structure of the activated RET signaling complex reveals the importance of its cysteine-rich domain; Structure and biophysical characterization of the human full-length neurturin-GFRa2 complex: A role for heparan sulfate in signaling
decision_basis: The reviews identify GFRα2 as the preferred neurturin co-receptor for RET; primary cryo-EM and structural/biophysical studies reconstitute NRTN/GFRα2/RET interfaces and show that complex formation supports RET dimerization and activation.
limitations_preserved: Preserve NRTN homodimer, GPI-linked GFRα2 co-receptor, RET tripartite/heterohexameric topology, and heparan-sulfate/avidity context; NCAM is an alternative receptor branch; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2884560, GDNF family; PMCID:PMC7377943, The role of glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor family member artemin in neurological disorders and cancers
primary_title: Artemin, a novel member of the GDNF ligand family, supports peripheral and central neurons and signals through the GFRalpha3-RET receptor complex; Quantitative analysis of the activation mechanism of the multicomponent growth-factor receptor Ret; Structure of artemin complexed with its receptor GFRalpha3: convergent recognition of glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factors
decision_basis: The reviews identify GFRα3 as the preferred artemin co-receptor for RET; primary neuronal, quantitative live-cell, and structural studies show ARTN/GFRα3-dependent RET complex formation, RET phosphorylation/activation, and neuronal survival or receptor-proximal responses.
limitations_preserved: Preserve ARTN homodimer, preferred GFRα3 specificity with documented alternative GFRα1 activity, RET tripartite topology, and neuronal/heterologous context; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6080411, Revisiting Netrin-1: One Who Guides (Axons); PMCID:PMC5372507, Role of Netrin-1 Signaling in Nerve Regeneration
primary_title: Endothelial Unc5B controls blood-brain barrier integrity
decision_basis: The reviews identify UNC5 receptors as netrin-1 repulsive/vascular receptor partners; the primary endothelial study demonstrates Netrin-1/UNC5B ligand-receptor function, UNC5B-dependent Wnt/β-catenin barrier regulation, and blockade-sensitive blood-brain-barrier integrity.
limitations_preserved: Preserve endothelial UNC5B and BBB/Wnt-context boundaries, antibody-blockade and in vivo perturbation semantics, and netrin-1 receptor-family specificity; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3389612, Receptor complexes for each of the Class 3 Semaphorins; PMCID:PMC7409005, Characterization of Class-3 Semaphorin Receptors, Neuropilins and Plexins
primary_title: Plexin-neuropilin-1 complexes form functional semaphorin-3A receptors; Semaphorin3A, Neuropilin-1, and PlexinA1 are required for lymphatic valve formation
decision_basis: The reviews identify NRP1/plexin-A complexes as functional SEMA3A receptors; primary biochemical and developmental studies show stable NRP1/PLXNA1 complex formation, SEMA3A binding, growth-cone/cell-shape responses, and NRP1/PLXNA1-dependent lymphatic-valve function.
limitations_preserved: Preserve NRP1 ligand-binding and PLXNA1 signal-transducing subunit roles, multimeric semaphorin/plexin avidity, species and sensory/lymphatic context; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3389612, Receptor complexes for each of the Class 3 Semaphorins; PMCID:PMC4980550, Structural Basis for Plexin Activation and Regulation
primary_title: Neuropilins lock secreted semaphorins onto plexins in a ternary signaling complex; Plexin/neuropilin complexes mediate repulsion by the axonal guidance signal semaphorin 3A
decision_basis: The reviews identify NRP1 and class-A plexins as the multicomponent SEMA3A receptor; primary structural and cellular studies resolve SEMA3A/PLXNA2/NRP1 interfaces and show NRP1-stabilized plexin interaction and semaphorin-dependent receptor signaling.
limitations_preserved: Preserve NRP1 cross-brace/co-receptor role, PLXNA2 signal-transducing context, semaphorin dimer avidity, and structural/cellular assay boundaries; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.
